title: Reliability-based chance-constrained control for suppressing parametric oscillations in multi-timescale gas turbine systems
abstract: Within the automatic control mode of gas turbines, ubiquitous parametric oscillations arise from periodic and stochastic operational excitations in a multi-timescale coupled nonlinear gas-path system (MN-GPS), thereby posing a severe threat to operational safety. To elucidate the formation mechanisms of these oscillations and propose a robust suppression control strategy, this study introduces a reliability-based chance-constrained control and develops a comprehensive model integrating gas-path, mechanical, and hydraulic subsystems with dead-band effects. The excitation of fuel system was extracted from operational data and incorporated into MN-GPS model, which was validated by steady-state and transient operating data under different conditions. The proportional gain under different time-scaling factors exhibits supercritical pitchfork bifurcation, and the transition between stable and extreme parametric oscillation has a step characteristic. Fast-slow timescale convergence induces extreme instability events that dramatically reduce operational reliability. Both the degree and time delay of stability margin are significantly influenced by nonlinear dead-band effects during dynamic operation process. Based on the parameter oscillation state transition law, a fast compensator based on reliability-based chance constraints was designed to suppress parameter oscillations, and its effectiveness was verified through comparisons with methods such as ADRC and LSTM-NN. The comparative simulation and Hardware-in-the-Loop testing results show that the proposed method can effectively suppress extreme oscillations under continuous excitation and maintain the system operating in a high-reliability region. This work provides solutions for parameter oscillation risk suppression and operation reliability optimization in multi-scale nonlinear industrial systems.

title: A hybrid fractional-order PID-PSO adaptive token bucket architecture for resilient IoT supply chain security
venue: Engineering Science and Technology, an International Journal
abstract: The rapid integration of Internet of Things (IoT) devices into industrial supply chains exposes embedded gateways to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks that can destabilize latency-sensitive industrial processes. This paper introduces a hybrid Fractional-Order PID (FOPID) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) Token Bucket architecture implemented at the XDP (eXpress Data Path) native hook, the earliest programmable point in the Linux kernel. The FOPID controller dynamically adjusts the Token Bucket replenishment rate using real-time network throughput and traffic statistics, enabling proportional rate regulation that helps preserve legitimate bursty flows while mitigating malicious traffic. A trigger-driven PSO layer, activated only when stability thresholds are violated, tunes the five FOPID gains by minimizing the Integrated Time Absolute Error (ITAE) criterion. The optimized parameters are transmitted to the kernel-space FOPID controller via eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) maps, allowing low-latency control updates with limited runtime overhead. The control mechanism uses a fixed control-sampling period to support timely adaptation while maintaining the timing constraints of the target cyber-physical setting. Experimental results on a physical IoT warehouse testbed show that the proposed architecture improves both resilience and service stability under multi-vector attacks. Relative to the standard Token Bucket, the method reduced packet loss by 7.7–18.5%, and compared with iptables hashlimit, it lowered CPU utilization by 10–30%. Under Layer 7 flooding, it constrained P99 latency to 132.90 ms.

title: Ghost imaging-based lightweight encryption scheme with auxiliary probe verification for industrial inspection robots
abstract: In the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), drone-based industrial inspection robots have been widely deployed, posing significant challenges to the secure transmission of industrial vision data. This paper proposes a lightweight industrial vision encryption scheme based on computational ghost imaging (CGI) with auxiliary probe verification. First, a novel 3D memristor-modulated hyperchaotic map (3D-MMHM) is developed as the core encryption engine. Lyapunov exponent spectra, bifurcation analysis, and NIST randomness tests demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits excellent unpredictability and a large key space. Based on the 3D-MMHM, a dual-track encryption framework is constructed. The main track integrates CGI-inspired global pixel permutation with dynamically cascaded diffusion chains to enhance resistance against chosen-plaintext attacks, while the auxiliary track employs a lightweight CGI-based auxiliary probe mechanism to intercept abnormal packets prior to decryption, thereby reducing unnecessary computational overhead under channel interference. Security performance evaluations show that the NPCR and UACI values reach 99.61% and 33.46%, while the ciphertext entropy approaches 8.0. Moreover, the proposed scheme achieves an encryption throughput of up to 3578.60 KB/s for high-resolution industrial images, demonstrating strong potential for real-time visual data protection in harsh industrial environments.

title: Recent advances on performance enhancement techniques of phase change materials for energy storage system: a review
abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) are promising mediums for high-density thermal energy storage (HTES), and have the potential to become important and useful in the fields of concentrated solar power, industrial waste heat recovery, and advanced thermal management systems. The very low thermal conductivity, however, is an intrinsic property that limits heat transfer rates and system efficiency. This review provides a critical, multi-scale synthesis of recent advances in latent heat thermal energy storage (LHTES) materials, structures, and systems, focusing on material modification, structural design, and system optimization. The major enhancement strategies are the integration of porous media (such as metal foams and expanded graphite), the incorporation of carbon-based and metal/metal oxide nanoparticles as nano-enhanced PCM, the introduction of the encapsulation technique to enhance the stability and leakage prevention, and the modification of the structure by the use of fins and heat pipes. At the system level, cascaded PCM configurations, along with active enhancement techniques such as rotation, vibration, and multi-field, are demonstrated to significantly improve heat transfer, temperature uniformity, and charging, discharging performance. The analysis uncovers key challenges and trade-offs, including nanoparticle instability, declining latent heat, the lack of widely accepted evaluation frameworks, and the need for long-term validation. It is suggested that future research should focus on application-specific, integrated design strategies, with standardized benchmarking, advanced optimization, and field validation, to facilitate the deployment of PCM-based thermal energy storage systems on a larger scale and at a lower cost.

title: Electromagnetically reshaped nonlinear stiffness through a 2-DoF X-mechanism for coupled vibration isolation
abstract: With a new concept, nonlinear reshaping, this study presents a novel electromagnetically reshaped X-structured platform, engineered to tackle the persistent challenge of adaptive vibration isolation specifically for coupled vertical–rotational excitations and variable payloads. Evolving from a previous X-mechanism, our design incorporates two pivotal modifications: released constraints at the central joint to introduce a new rotational degree of freedom (DoF), and integrated bilateral rhombic substructures coupled with a custom electromagnetic actuator. This synthesis enables combined vertical–rotational motion and provides a robust foundation for active stiffness modulation. Crucially, we demonstrate that the system's intrinsic nonlinear stiffness, which generates a tunable quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) region, can be dynamically reshaped by the actuator's Lorentz force, bypassing the need for mechanical reconfiguration. Finite element analysis validates the actuator's linear thrust-current relationship and precise force–displacement profile. Dynamic modeling via Lagrange's equations and the harmonic balance method reveals that this electromagnetic control effectively separates closely spaced resonance peaks under complex coupled excitations. Experimental validation and comparative studies with a functional prototype confirm the platform's exceptional adaptability. For payloads varying in mass and moment of inertia both up to 100%, the system maintains a stable resonance frequency at 1.5±0.5 Hz and delivers consistent, robust vibration isolation performance. This work provides a practical and efficient solution for protecting sensitive equipment in dynamic environments, such as aerospace vehicles and precision manufacturing systems, where both the payload and the vibrational landscape are subject to significant change.

title: Benchmarking zero-shot vision-language models against supervised learning for concurrent metabolic rate and clothing insulation estimation
abstract: With individuals spending more than 85% of their time indoors, maintaining Thermal Comfort (TC) is essential for well-being and energy efficiency. While the Predicted Mean Vote (PMV) index is the standard metric, its accuracy suffers when personal factors, specifically Metabolic Rate (MET) and Clothing Insulation (CLO), are treated as constant values. Recent advances in Computer Vision (CV) offer a non-intrusive method to estimate these parameters, yet progress is hindered by the scarcity of privacy-compliant, granular real-world datasets. We introduce a novel high-fidelity synthetic dataset generated via Unreal Engine 5 (UE5), featuring 2250 video clips with expert-annotated ground truth for MET and CLO aligned with ASHRAE Standard 55. Leveraging this dataset, we present the first comprehensive benchmark comparing a specialized supervised model against state-of-the-art (SOTA) zero-shot Vision-Language Models (VLMs). We propose a modified pretrained multi-task Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture as a supervised baseline and contrast it with the flagship Gemini 3 Pro and the lightweight 2.5 Flash using a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategy. Results indicate that zero-shot Gemini 3 Pro significantly outperforms the CNN baseline in semantic accuracy, achieving Mean Absolute Errors (MAEs) of 0.31 MET and 0.021 CLO. Conversely, latency analysis identifies the multi-task CNN as the most viable option for high-frequency control loops due to its 3.93-second inference latency per clip, while Gemini 2.5 Flash provides a balanced, accessible alternative for periodic building adjustments. This study validates the utility of synthetic digital occupants for benchmarking AI models, enabling a scalable, privacy-preserving Occupant Centric Control (OCC) pipeline.

title: A scenario-driven review of multi-agent cooperation for lunar surface missions
abstract: The transition from short-term lunar sorties to sustained International Lunar Research Station calls for multi-agent cooperative systems. However, terrestrial swarm paradigms face a severe reality gap under lunar constraints in communication, SWaP, and radiation-hardened computing. This systematic review organizes lunar multi-agent research using a new operational taxonomy spanning three mission phases and a six-domain cooperative technical framework, and assesses validation readiness via an Evidence Maturity scale (L0–L4). Our evidence-weighted synthesis shows a bifurcated maturity landscape: while foundational exploration and mapping architectures have achieved L3 validation in terrestrial planetary analogs, actual lunar flight deployments (L4) remain absent, and research into construction, logistics, and maintenance is critically sparse. Our synthesis further reveals that validated systems consistently adopt hybrid modular architectures with communication-aware planning and human-on-the-loop supervision, while fully decentralized end-to-end learning paradigms remain confined to simulation. We further expose an assumption gap between algorithmic prerequisites and lunar physical reality. To narrow the sim-to-real chasm, we identify transferable methods from deep-space learning and in-orbit servicing, and propose a roadmap emphasizing communication autonomy, task self-organization, and engineering realism.

title: Design of a liquid state space model proportional–integral– derivative controller for generator oscillation suppression in power cyber-physical systems
abstract: Under short-circuit fault conditions in power cyber-physical systems, generator oscillations pose a serious threat to safe and stable operation. This study proposes a hybrid controller—the Liquid State Space Model Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller—that integrates a Liquid State Space Model with conventional Proportional–Integral–Derivative control. By selecting suitable state matrices to represent the controlled plant's state information, the Liquid State Space Model produces effective parameter updates for the Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller. Leveraging the Liquid State Space Model's ability to handle sequential data and to dynamically adjust its state transition matrix, the proposed controller enables real-time adaptive tuning of Proportional–Integral–Derivative gains. We apply the Liquid State Space Model Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller to a Single Machine Infinite Bus power cyber-physical system. Simulation experiments evaluate its ability to suppress generator oscillations, benchmarked against a Backpropagation Neural Network Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller, a Recurrent Neural Network Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller, and a no-controller baseline, under short-circuit faults and communication-layer network interference. For example, under a three-phase short-circuit fault with a 2-ms disturbance, the Liquid State Space Model Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller achieves an overshoot of 1.154079, outperforming the Backpropagation Neural Network Proportional–Integral–Derivative (3.294508) and the Recurrent Neural Network Proportional–Integral–Derivative (1.504131) and delivering the best overall control performance among the tested methods. Overall, results show that the Liquid State Space Model Proportional–Integral–Derivative controller provides stronger oscillation suppression and faster recovery across all tested conditions, confirming its effectiveness for complex dynamic systems.

title: Fog-Quant: A quantum computing inspired framework for fog computing deployment over 6G radio access networks
abstract: Future 6G networks promise revolutionary capabilities with terabit speeds and sub-millisecond latency. However, achieving these goals requires fundamental changes in how we manage computing resources. Traditional cloud architectures cannot meet 6G's strict timing requirements because data must travel too far to distant servers. Fog computing brings processing power closer to users by embedding micro data centers in cell towers and street infrastructure. Yet current fog orchestration methods struggle with 6G's unique challenges. Terahertz frequencies suffer severe signal degradation. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces need constant adjustment as users move. Managing thousands of diverse fog nodes while optimizing latency, energy, and resource usage becomes impossibly complex for classical algorithms. This paper introduces Fog-Quant, the first quantum-powered orchestration system designed specifically for 6G fog networks. Our framework combines two quantum algorithms to solve placement problems that defeat traditional methods. Quantum Annealing rapidly explores millions of possible solutions in microseconds. The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm then refines these solutions with mathematical precision. Fog-Quant uses intelligent entropy-based decision making. Simple placement choices use fast classical methods. Complex scenarios activate quantum processing. This adaptive approach ensures optimal performance without wasting computational resources. We evaluated Fog Quant on a calibrated emulation testbed with 10,000 fog nodes and 10,000 microservices. Fog Quant reaches 96.1 percent placement success at 10,000 nodes and reduces energy use by 28.8 percent versus classical baselines. It maintains reliability above 99.995 percent with up to 30 percent node unavailability. Over 90 percent of control loop events finish within 2.2 ms, with a 2.16 ms decision time bound, meeting a 10 ms URLLC requirement in dense urban scenarios.

title: Robust multimodal latent repair for fault-tolerant cyber–physical production systems
abstract: Multimodal fusion systems in industrial environments are critically vulnerable to sensor faults that destabilize downstream tasks. In capital-intensive sectors such as automotive manufacturing and aerospace, these unmitigated failures translate directly into substantial financial losses due to unplanned downtime and catastrophic equipment damage. To address this, we introduce a mathematically grounded framework for robust multimodal latent repair, which fundamentally re-engineers the Transformer block for fault tolerance. We derive a spectral decomposition proving that residual connections preserve fault locality while attention heads diffuse it. Leveraging this orthogonality, we propose the residual-contrastive attention module. This mechanism utilizes a novel local–global ratio to explicitly detect anomalies and employs an inverse-residual gate to suppress and inpaint corrupted tokens using global context. Validated on rigorous industrial digital twins, our model-based approach achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity, providing a deterministic architectural guarantee of error containment that effectively decouples physical sensor degradation from operational system stability without relying on implicit regularization.

title: High-performance fixed-time active fault-tolerant control for robotic manipulators via sparse physics-informed dynamics learning
abstract: High-precision tracking of robotic manipulators is challenged by nonlinear friction, model mismatch, external disturbances, and abrupt actuator faults. Conventional robust controllers often lump these effects into a single uncertainty, resulting in conservative gains and high control effort. This paper develops a novel fixed-time active fault-tolerant control (AFTC) framework that couples sparse physics-informed dynamics learning with fixed-time robust compensation. A physics-informed neural network with sparse regression (PINN–SR) learns the physics gap between the nominal model and the plant and identifies parsimonious, interpretable terms for friction and structured uncertainties. A fixed-time fault observer then reconstructs the remaining lumped perturbations, including actuator faults, disturbances, and residual approximation errors. Using these compensations, a novel nonsingular fixed-time sliding-mode controller with a state-dependent exponent and hyperbolic-secant gain guarantees convergence within a settling-time bound independent of initial conditions; fixed-time stability is proven via Lyapunov analysis. MATLAB/Simulink–Simscape simulations of a 3-DOF SAMSUNG FARA AT2 manipulator against five recent controllers show improved performance. In the fault-free case, convergence time is 0.276–0.322 s, and the integral absolute error is 0.0186–0.0506rad (38–42% and approximately 40% improvements over the best baseline results, respectively). Under actuator faults, the proposed method further reduces the tracking error by 41–51% while preserving smooth control inputs.

title: Nonlinear bidirectional dynamic latent modeling for closed-loop process monitoring
abstract: Closed-loop control brings new challenges for process monitoring. Nonlinearities in the correlation structure and the dynamic relations in closed-loop process data further complicate the task. To tackle these issues, a new dynamic latent variable scheme is proposed in this paper for nonlinear closed-loop processes. The nonlinearities of the processes are investigated in detail first, followed by a dynamic latent variable object for latent structure extraction of nonlinear closed-loop processes. An algorithm is then proposed to solve the constructed optimization object which has guaranteed convergency. The relations of the extracted dynamic latent model are revealed in detail afterwards, and the process monitoring strategy is built with comprehensive analysis of variations in closed-loop process data. A numerical simulation and a study on the thruster system of the “Jiaolong” deep-sea submarine are carried on to show the performance of the proposed scheme.

title: Learning-based fault-tolerant control for flexible joint robotic manipulators: An actor-critic framework with experimental verification
abstract: Flexible-joint robotic manipulators (FJRMs) offer significant advantages over traditional rigid-link counterparts, including improved dexterity, greater motion flexibility, and lower energy consumption. However, their control remains challenging due to inherent nonlinear dynamics, elastic joint coupling, external disturbances, and susceptibility to actuator faults. This paper presents a Lyapunov-guided actor-critic reinforcement learning (RL) fault-tolerant control strategy for FJRMs. Different from conventional adaptive neural-network control, where the neural network is mainly used as a direct uncertainty approximator, the proposed method introduces a critic network to learn the long-run cost-to-go from tracking error, control effort, and fault-induced performance degradation, and uses this critic evaluation to guide actor policy improvement online. The Lyapunov design supplies a stabilizing control structure, while the actor-critic learning mechanism provides value-based policy adaptation under unknown matched uncertainties and actuator faults. Semi-global uniform ultimate boundedness of all closed-loop signals is established, and experiments on a Baxter robotic platform demonstrate improved tracking accuracy and robustness compared with PID and single neural-network controllers under faulty conditions.

title: Adaptive dynamic programming-based fault tolerant control for nonlinear time-delay systems
abstract: This study introduces a fault compensation control approach for a class of affine nonlinear time-delay systems using adaptive dynamic programming (ADP). By establishing an observer, the ADP-derived approach facilitates the estimation of potential actuator faults within the system. A novel value function is devised to incorporate the estimated fault and state delay. Subsequently, the control laws are derived from this innovative value function. The Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation associated with this innovative value function is effectively solved using a critic neural network. Then, it is demonstrated through Lyapunov theory that the closed-loop systems achieve uniform ultimate boundedness. The efficacy of the current fault compensation strategy is validated through simulation instances. A notable contribution of the proposed method is its extension of the ADP technique to address the challenge of fault compensation in nonlinear time-delay systems.

title: KPCA digital twin-enhanced real-time fault-tolerant control for autonomous vehicles
abstract: Fault-tolerant control for autonomous vehicles is challenged by sensor degradation, actuator failures, and the need for real-time fault reconstruction without interrupting operation. This paper proposes an integrated framework combining Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) digital twin technology with Model Predictive Control (MPC) to enable unified fault detection, estimation, and real-time reconstruction. The KPCA digital twin uses kernel-based nonlinear dimensionality reduction to model complex fault dynamics in high-dimensional sensor and actuator data, facilitating effective decomposition of multivariate fault patterns. Adaptive Kalman filtering (AKF) and probabilistic signal smoothing enhance fault reconstruction while maintaining continuous control performance. The framework is supported by rigorous mathematical foundations, ensuring stability and convergence of the kernel-based algorithms. Leveraging kernel methods’ universal approximation capabilities, it achieves superior fault tolerance with real-time computational efficiency. Experimental validation shows 98.2 % fault detection accuracy across multiple sensor and actuator failure scenarios. Multi-scenario testing reveals significant improvements over uncompensated faults, including 90.5 % velocity error reduction, 91.7 % lateral error improvement, and 81.1 % angular error reduction. Compared to existing approaches focused on detection-only or requiring system interruption, this framework provides seamless real-time fault reconstruction. A comparative study against 14 state-of-the-art methods highlights its advantages in integrated control-diagnosis, nonlinear modeling, and continuous operation. This KPCA Digital Twin MPC framework establishes a new paradigm for fault-tolerant control in autonomous vehicles, bridging digital twin technology with practical, safety–critical applications.

title: Fault-tolerant control for micro-reactor sensors based on a PMSDC-LSTM-SE framework
abstract: This paper proposes a fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control framework for sensor failures in micro-reactor systems. A sensor reconstruction model based on a Parallel Multi-Scale Dilated Convolutional Network (PMSDC), Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM), and Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) channel attention mechanism is developed to reconstruct faulty sensor measurements from raw multivariate time-series signals. The reconstruction residual between the measured and estimated values is evaluated using Bayesian estimation to identify sensor faults and reduce false detection. The proposed selective Bayesian residual detection method achieves a false alarm rate of 0.00%, demonstrating improved reliability in distinguishing normal and faulty sensor states. After fault diagnosis, the faulty sensor is isolated and replaced with a redundant sensor to maintain control performance. Experimental results on a micro-reactor fault dataset demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies sensor fault types and severities, achieving average reductions of 53.5% in RMSE and 52.6% in MAE compared with the CNN-LSTM-based reconstruction approach. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for sensor fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control in micro-reactor systems.

title: Layer-specific lipschitz modulation for fault-tolerant multimodal representation learning
abstract: Modern multimodal systems deployed in industrial and safety-critical environments must remain reliable under partial sensor failures, signal degradation, or cross-modal inconsistencies. This work introduces a mathematically grounded framework for fault-tolerant multimodal representation learning that unifies self-supervised anomaly detection and error correction within a single architecture. Building upon a theoretical analysis of perturbation propagation, we derive Lipschitz- and Jacobian-based criteria that determine whether a neural operator amplifies or attenuates localized faults. Guided by this theory, we propose a two-stage self-supervised training scheme: pre-training a multimodal convolutional autoencoder on clean data to preserve localized anomaly signals in the latent space, and expanding it with a learnable compute block composed of dense layers for correction and contrastive objectives for anomaly identification. Furthermore, we introduce layer-specific Lipschitz modulation and gradient clipping as principled mechanisms to control sensitivity across detection and correction modules. Experimental results on multimodal fault datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach improves both anomaly detection accuracy and reconstruction under sensor corruption. Overall, this framework bridges the gap between analytical robustness guarantees and practical fault-tolerant multimodal learning.

title: Dynamic memory event-triggered optimized containment control of nonlinear MASs with actuator faults
abstract: This paper investigates the optimized containment control problem of nonlinear multi-agent systems with actuator faults. To address the optimized control problem, a neural network-based reinforcement learning strategy is proposed, employing the identifier-critic-actor architecture and backstepping framework. The critic and actor update laws are reformulated through the negative gradients of a simple positive function, thereby bypassing the computational intractability of solving the nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman partial differential equation and eliminating the need for persistent external incentives. Furthermore, for the actuator faults including partial loss of effectiveness and lock-in-place, a fault-tolerant control scheme that compensates for actuator faults via the adaptive law is integrated into the optimized controller. In addition, to reduce the communication burden, a dynamic memory event-triggered mechanism is introduced. This mechanism incorporates a time-delay term to account for the influence of historical information on triggering conditions, thereby effectively reducing the waste of communication resources. In view of Lyapunov stability theory, it is proved that all signals in the closed-loop system are bounded and the outputs of all followers converge to the convex hull formed by the leaders. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control scheme are demonstrated through a simulation example.

title: A meta Proximal policy optimization driven task interaction graph scheduler with predictive resource provisioning and fault-tolerant micro-checkpointing for adaptive spark workflow scheduling in multi-cloud systems
abstract: Efficient task scheduling in Spark workflows across heterogeneous multi-cloud environments remains a critical challenge due to dynamic resource availability, unstable virtual machine (VM) performance, and demand for cross-cloud fault tolerance. Existing approaches often depend on static heuristics or reinforcement learning models that require extensive retraining, limiting adaptability and scalability. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes Meta-Proximal Policy Optimization-driven Task Interaction Graph Scheduler (Meta-PPO-TIGS), a framework for adaptive, efficient, and fault-tolerant Spark workflow scheduling. The proposed framework applies Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically Meta-Reinforcement Learning through Meta-Proximal Policy Optimization (Meta-PPO), to optimize task scheduling, resource provisioning, and fault recovery in heterogeneous multi-cloud computing environments. Meta-PPO-TIGS models Spark jobs as Task Interaction Graphs (TIGs) and integrates three modules: a Context-Aware Elastic Resource Manager (CAERM) for predictive resource provisioning, a Variance-Aware Performance Monitor (VAPM) for VM stability monitoring and task remapping, and a Replicated Micro-Checkpointing Layer (RMCL) for lightweight cross-cloud fault tolerance. Leveraging Meta-PPO, the scheduler rapidly adapts to unseen workflow types and heterogeneous cloud conditions without retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Meta-PPO-TIGS achieves lower makespans, resource utilization, reduced fault recovery time and improved cost-efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show an average execution time of 820 s, resource utilization of 85%, task remapping frequency of 12, checkpointing overhead of 45 s, fault recovery time of 60 s, and latency of 120 ms. Furthermore, cost efficiency is improved with 5.0% Relative Percentage Deviation (RPD). These findings confirm that Meta-PPO-TIGS provides a robust, adaptive, scalable solution for next-generation multi-cloud workflow scheduling.

title: Intelligent inversion and fault-tolerant localization method for subsea manifold leakage based on physical consistency
abstract: The subsea manifold is a core component of subsea production systems, and its reliability directly affects production efficiency. To address leakage localization under abnormal conditions such as sensor failure, a physics-consistent intelligent inversion and fault-tolerant localization method is proposed. First, a nonlinear attenuation model for leakage-induced dynamic pressure signals is established, and multi-stage noise separation and hybrid parameter identification are performed to enhance leakage feature extraction under interference. Subsequently, multimodal features are extracted using a sliding-window strategy to construct a high-dimensional feature space for characterizing the dynamic responses of leakage events. Finally, a feature-enhanced physics-informed neural network is developed, in which a customized physics-constrained loss function and a two-stage training strategy are introduced to coordinate data-driven learning with physical consistency. Guided by the physics-constrained loss function, the spatial mapping of leakage locations is learned from the integrated features of the remaining valid sensor signals, rather than from a single sensor or a fixed sensor set. Experimental results show that the average localization error is only 6.63 cm under the complete-sensor condition and is limited to 15.48 cm even when four sensor signals are missing, indicating that the proposed method maintains high localization accuracy under incomplete sensor information.

title: Robust adaptive <ce:italic>H</ce:italic><ce:inf loc=post>∞</ce:inf> fault-tolerant predictive control for air-ground integrated highway emergency self-organizing network systems based on RBF-DNN approximation
abstract: Road traffic safety remains a critical challenge for public safety governance, and highway emergencies demand rapid, reliable communication and decision support. For air-ground integrated wireless ad-hoc networks in such scenarios, existing fault-tolerant control schemes rarely address the coupled effects of highly time-varying channels, packet loss, actuator/sensor degradation, and accident risk prediction within a unified framework. This paper proposes a robust adaptive H∞ fault-tolerant predictive control method incorporating RBF-DNN (Radial Basis Function-Deep Neural Network) approximation for a two-layer heterogeneous “UAV-road” network. A networked control model integrating link quality, queue evolution, and resource execution constraints is constructed, and an RBF-DNN is employed for online approximation of unknown nonlinearities and unmodeled dynamics. An adaptive law with projection and σ[jls-end-space/]-modification is developed to suppress parameter drift, and an event-triggered communication mechanism is introduced to reduce overhead and avoid Zeno behavior. Within a Lyapunov framework, we rigorously establish bounded stability and an H∞ performance upper bound for the closed-loop system under link failures, random packet loss, and partial actuator/sensor faults. Simulation results show that, under sudden link interruptions, 40–50 % packet loss and 75 % actuator performance degradation, the proposed controller maintains QoS and prescribed γ[jls-end-space/]-level H∞ performance with asymptotic state convergence. On a real S103 highway dataset (372 samples, 10.8 % positives), the associated accident risk prediction module achieves 70–75 % test accuracy with PR-AUC is 0.683 and ROC-AUC is 0.715, demonstrating practically useful high-risk segment discrimination under severe class imbalance and confirming the engineering feasibility of the proposed control prediction framework.

title: Workload-aware approximate backup to reduce fault-tolerant overhead for stream processing applications
abstract: Distributed Stream Processing Systems (DSPSs) are powering big data applications on high-velocity data streams. Compared to offline data processing models, stream processing is more susceptible to failures in the face of on-the-fly data and large distributed cluster deployment. A variety of fault-tolerant techniques have emerged to achieve the reliability of DSPSs, and checkpoint-based approaches that periodically persist operator state are the most popular. However, making DSPSs with complete backup while retaining system performance is an open challenge: the shorter the recovery time from failure, the greater the runtime overhead due to frequent checkpoint operations. Meanwhile, more stream processing applications aim for fast results by allowing a slight degradation of output inaccuracy.This paper proposes a workload-aware approximate backup approach (WAFP), which provides an adaptive backup strategy to accommodate the data dynamics of the online stream application. It enables lower fault tolerance overhead while maintaining a given output accuracy. Considering single-node failure and correlated failure scenarios, we design two algorithms to generate a proper backup plan accordingly. Extensive experiments have been conducted on our simulator, demonstrating that the proposed method achieves substantial improvements over previous methods. The results confirm that our solution ensures the minimum fault-tolerant latency with a given output accuracy for the single-node scenario.

title: Reinforcement learning based self-triggered sliding mode fault-tolerant control for underwater vehicles
abstract: In this paper, an observer-based fault-tolerant control using reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed for an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) equipped with a bow rudder and four independent stern rudders arranged in an X-configuration. To enable real-time fault detection, an integrated adaptive second-order sliding mode observer is employed to estimate rudder effectiveness factors online. Based on the observer’s fault indicators, an Actor-Critic RL-based controller is trained to adaptively generate fault-compensating control inputs by minimizing tracking errors under fault conditions. To alleviate computational burden and decrease control update frequency, a self-triggered strategy is introduced, and the triggering condition is defined by both trajectory tracking errors and fault detection indicators. Finally, the fault-compensating control signals are mapped by bounded nonlinear transformation and integrated with pseudo-inverse allocation to ensure the actuator feasibility and admissibility. Results of numerical simulations and real experiments demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method, maintaining the robust tracking performance under actuator faults. The proposed method achieves a 55.8 % reduction in lateral tracking error and a 28.1 % decrease in control energy consumption under two-rudder faults, relative to conventional pseudoinverse allocation.

title: Actuator fault-tolerant control of underwater vehicle using koopman framework
abstract: Underwater Vehicles (UVs) face a high risk of mission failure or loss due to unknown onboard component faults, making prompt fault detection and mitigation crucial for operational safety. A novel, data-driven, active fault-tolerant control framework to address the challenge of unknown actuator faults in UVs is proposed. The core of the framework is the Koopman operator, which identifies the UV’s system dynamics directly from operational input-output data collected during trajectory tracking via a backstepping controller. This data yields a linear Koopman operator used to design a linear observer for real-time fault detection and isolation. Once a fault is estimated, the framework achieves fault-tolerant control by reconfiguring the existing controller. The whole framework is successfully demonstrated on a fixed 8-thruster underwater vehicle, effectively detecting and compensating for injected actuator faults. The results showcase that the proposed Koopman-based active fault-tolerant control offers a promising, data-driven solution that significantly enhances the reliability and operational safety of underwater vehicles in real-world environments.

title: Transformer-based fault-tolerant control for fixed-wing aerial vehicles using offline reinforcement learning
abstract: This study presents a transformer-based approach for fault-tolerant control in fixed-wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), designed to adapt in real time to dynamic changes caused by structural damage or actuator failures. Unlike traditional Flight Control Systems (FCSs) that rely on classical control theory and struggle under severe alterations in dynamics, our method directly maps outer-loop reference values (altitude, heading, and airspeed) into control commands using the in-context learning and attention mechanisms of transformers, thus bypassing inner-loop controllers and fault-detection layers. Employing a teacher-student knowledge distillation framework, the proposed approach trains a student agent with partial observations by transferring knowledge from a privileged expert agent with full observability, enabling robust performance across diverse failure scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our transformer-based controller outperforms industry-standard FCS and state-of-the-art reinforcement learning (RL) methods, maintaining high tracking accuracy and reliable flight behavior in nominal conditions and extreme failure cases, highlighting its potential for enhancing UAV operational safety and reliability. youtu.be/ATW3LZFRqc0

title: A hybrid fault-tolerant control allocation for an over-actuated USV with azimuth thruster saturation: Experimental system identification and HITL validation
abstract: This study proposes a hybrid fault-tolerance control allocation framework combining quadratic programming (QP) and redistributed pseudo-inverse (RPI) methods for an over-actuated unmanned surface vehicle (USV). The system consists of eight actuators, including four rotational thrusters and four azimuth servos, all subject to physical saturation constraints. Hydrodynamic parameters are identified from experimental data using a maximum likelihood output error method, yielding a physically consistent model suitable for control-oriented applications. Based on an autonomous mission generated by path planning, a line-of-sight (LOS) guidance scheme and motion controllers are developed to produce the desired generalized forces and moments. A mode-dependent allocation strategy is employed, where QP is used in position-critical phases to explicitly handle constraints, while RPI ensures computational efficiency during waypoint-following and docking-approach phases. A fault-tolerant mechanism is further incorporated to reconfigure the control allocation under actuator failure conditions. Both simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable autonomous mission completion with improved tracking performance and efficient actuator utilization under both nominal and faulty scenarios.

title: Intelligent hybrid neural network-reinforcement learning framework for fault-tolerant formation control
abstract: This study presents an intelligent hybrid control framework that integrates a Neural Network–based Fault and Disturbance Observer (FDO) with a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) controller to enhance autonomy and resilience in aerospace formation systems. The hybrid NN–DRL architecture replaces conventional model-based control with a learning-driven approach capable of real-time fault diagnosis, adaptive recovery, and stability preservation under uncertain flight conditions. The FDO provides high-accuracy fault estimation for actuator and dynamic anomalies, while the DRL agent learns optimal control strategies through Lyapunov-guided reward shaping to ensure Uniform Ultimate Boundedness (UUB) of formation-tracking errors. High-fidelity simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an average formation-tracking error of 0.17 m , fault-recovery within 1.6 s , and real-time implementation with a control update of only 2.3 ms . These results confirm superior fault tolerance, faster convergence, and improved reliability, offering a scalable solution for next-generation autonomous aerospace missions.

title: A latencies tolerant model predictive control approach to damp Inter-area oscillations in delayed power systems
venue: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
abstract: Automatic voltage regulators and power system stabilizers have been employed successfully to deal with fast dynamics associated to local oscillations phenomena. Whereas, inter-area oscillations damping in large power systems requires remote feedback controllers fed by Wide Area Monitoring Systems (WAMS). Although these improvements in the inter-area oscillations behavior have been effective, a new challenge emerges: reaching stability with a closed loop control despite latencies due to measurements taken far away from the control centre. The research was motivated by the need for modernization of power systems capable of dealing with control difficulties in centralised WAMS for damping inter-area oscillations in power systems caused by delays in the communication system. Herein, time delay and control problems are addressed separately. The time delay problem is solved by a database based time compensation solution relying on the most updated available state of the system. The control problem is solved by a Model Predictive Control (MPC) with terminal cost and constraint set to handle complexities due to nonlinearities of the power system, the large scale of the problem and the parametric variations. Both solutions work in a coordinated way with local controllers to implement a decentralised coordinated strategy that manages slow global dynamics and fast local dynamics as well. The integrated proposed approach is called Time-Delay-Tolerant Model Predictive Control (TDT-MPC). Coordinated and coherent performance of the two TDT-MPC components (Kalman compensator and MPC) is achieved thanks to unifying power system reference models for both strategies. The approach has been tested on the IEEE 39 system and validated with time domain nonlinear simulations, obtaining post-fault damped oscillations and a good tracking of new power references when tripping tie lines.

title: A robust fault-tolerant control algorithm for GPS-denied mini quadrotors using PID-TinyMPC and visual-inertial odometry
abstract: Fault-tolerant control (FTC) is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of autonomous quadrotors, especially in scenarios involving rotor failures. This paper presents a hybrid control architecture that combines a PID-based outer-loop controller with a TinyMPC-based inner-loop controller, integrated with visual-inertial odometry (VIO) for real-time state estimation. The proposed method enables a mini quadrotor to maintain stable flight and trajectory tracking even under rotor failure conditions, using only onboard sensors (IMU, barometer and monocular camera) without relying on external positioning systems such as GPS and VICON. The outer-loop PID controller handles position control at a lower frequency, while the inner-loop TinyMPC operates at a higher frequency to manage the fast-changing attitude dynamics. This design reduces computational overhead while maintaining spatial-temporal stability and precision. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in real-world scenarios, where the quadrotor successfully maintains hovering under varying yaw rates and rotor speed reduction conditions. The proposed low-cost, computationally efficient solution addresses a significant gap in the literature by providing a robust FTC approach that is feasible for microcontrollers and resource-constrained platforms. The source code and some flight videos are publicly available at: https://github.com/emrecintas/fault_tolerant_control.

title: Visualization analysis of research trends on thermal runaway warning of lithium-ion batteries: a bibliometric study
abstract: Lithium-ion battery thermal runaway warning (LIBTRW) is critical for ensuring the safety of electric vehicles and energy storage systems. From the Web of Science Core Collection database, this study systematically retrieves 1190 relevant articles published from 2003 to 2025. Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace, this study presents the first bibliometric analysis of LIBTRW research, including the development trends, research patterns, collaboration networks, publication sources, and citation characteristics. Keyword clustering and evolution path analysis are further performed to identify research hotspots and summarize mainstream early warning methods. The results reveal that the field has experienced an explosive growth since 2019. China dominates publication volume, while European and North American countries exhibit higher average citations per article. Tsinghua University and Beijing Institute of Technology are core research institutions. Scholars such as Ouyang MG, Feng XN, and Wang QS constitute the core author group. The Journal of Energy Storage, Journal of Power Sources, and Applied Energy are the primary publication sources. Research hotspots have shifted from early studies on thermal runaway mechanisms and temperature and voltage monitoring toward systematic directions, including multi-parameter fusion warning, gas sensing, and expansion force monitoring. Ten major research clusters are systematically identified, revealing a technological evolution path from mechanism elucidation to fault diagnosis and then to intelligent early warning. Based on these findings, future research should prioritize sensor reliability validation in real-world scenarios, robust deep learning methods with improved generalization, and module-level early warning testing to bridge the gap between academic research and engineering practice.

title: Multi-objective graph optimization for dynamic task–machine assignment in STEP-NC compliant smart factories using extended Floyd–Warshall algorithm
abstract: Future smart factories equipped with STEP-NC compliant machine tools promise a shift from machine-specific G-code to interoperable and feature-based manufacturing. While this enables unprecedented task assignment flexibility, it introduces a critical challenge in optimally allocating machining tasks across a heterogeneous and dynamic manufacturing floor. This limitation compromises factory resilience which can lead to accelerated resource wear, suboptimal throughput, and poor responsiveness to disruptions such as machine failures. To address this, we formulate the task-to-machine assignment as a multi-objective graph optimization problem. Our solution centers on an extended Floyd–Warshall algorithm that operates in a 4D state space by simultaneously evaluating task sequences, machine capabilities, and spatial constraints. This approach efficiently generates globally optimal manufacturing sequences that are both temporally efficient and physically executable. An empirical Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) surrogate testbed validates the approach by isolating and stress-testing the cyber–physical communication architecture under dynamic physical distress. Disruption scenarios confirmed the system's self-healing capability and demonstrated autonomous recovery from cascading hardware faults with a proven median latency of <1.5 s. Furthermore, 10 ms edge-level safety reflexes successfully protect physical nodes from severe parameter fluctuations, enforcing a “Correct-by-Construction” safety paradigm. Qualitatively, the framework provides factory managers with a highly tunable operational strategy to seamlessly shift between rush order processing and high-precision distributed routing while guaranteeing physical execution. By effectively transforming raw STEP-NC data into operationally feasible schedules that exhibit graceful degradation during disruptions, this work provides a critical step toward resilient and autonomous manufacturing systems capable of self-optimization in the face of dynamic change.

title: A review on cutting chatter detection and suppression in robotic milling
abstract: Robotic milling offers high manufacturing flexibility and reduced tooling costs for machining large, complex workpieces, but its inherently low structural stiffness makes it highly prone to cutting chatter. Chatter deteriorates surface quality and dimensional accuracy, accelerates tool wear, and may compromise robotic system safety. This review comprehensively examines cutting chatter in robotic milling, focusing on mechanisms, monitoring, and suppression strategies. First, it analyses robot-specific chatter mechanisms, including regenerative and modal coupling effects, posture-dependent compliant multi-body dynamics, and nonlinear chatter phenomena within unified rigid–flexible and multi-body dynamic frameworks. Second, chatter monitoring and diagnosis methods are summarised, spanning classical time–frequency and cyclostationary analysis to advanced data-driven and deep learning techniques, with emphasis on multi-sensor fusion and real-time edge deployment in robotic settings. Third, chatter suppression and control strategies are reviewed, covering machining parameter and robot pose optimisation, passive and active damping (e.g., tuned mass dampers, smart materials), and emerging reinforcement learning techniques and digital twin-based approaches. Unlike prior surveys focusing on conventional CNC machines or treating dynamics, detection, and control in isolation, this review uniquely addresses the interplay of posture-dependent robot dynamics with chatter across all stages. By highlighting distinctive challenges such as nonlinear chatter in compliant robotic systems and discussing state-of-the-art solutions, it clarifies research gaps and provides guidance for achieving stable, high-precision robotic milling.

title: Chapter 5: Artificial intelligence in cardiac drug delivery vehicles
venue: AI Powered Drug delivery to Neuro and Cardiovascular Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has begun to permeate the entire continuum of cardiac drug delivery, fusing data-driven molecular design, physiologically faithful simulation, and closed-loop control into therapeutic platforms capable of sensing, deciding, and acting within the dynamic heart. Machine-learning algorithms now screen polymers, lipids, and bioinspired membranes for optimal myocardial targeting; digital twins forecast nanocarrier dispersion across heterogeneous perfusion territories; reinforcement learners embedded in microrobots refine trajectories through pulsatile coronary flows; and responsive hydrogels modulate payload release when electrochemical cues signal ischemic stress. These converging innovations promise precision that static dosing regimens cannot approximate, yet they also expose fault lines: biased datasets threaten inequitable performance, algorithmic opacity complicates clinical trust, and legacy regulations struggle with adaptive software-hardware-pharma hybrids. The chapter dissects each technological stratum, from nanoparticle inverse design to AI-directed robotic actuators, while mapping the regulatory, ethical, and translational terrain that must be navigated before bedside adoption. Evidence from post-2020 trials illustrates tangible gains in anticoagulant titration, arrhythmia-responsive drug release, and risk-tailored stent aftercare, suggesting the first contours of a paradigm where cardiovascular therapy becomes a continuous dialogue between biological signal and computational response. What once resembled speculative fiction, microscale agents repairing myocardium under algorithmic guidance, now rests on demonstrable scientific foundations, pushing the field toward an era in which intelligent cardiotherapeutics are not ancillary aids but intrinsic partners in patient-specific care.

title: The skeletal connectome: From molecular circuitry to systemic network medicine
abstract: Although classically viewed as a mechanical scaffold, the skeleton is increasingly recognized as a dynamic endocrine and sensory hub that integrates systemic biophysical and biochemical cues. In this review, we rethink skeletal physiology by proposing the ‘skeletal connectome,’ a network medicine framework that links circuit-level remodeling programs to multiorgan homeostasis. Structurally, we first distill the cellular logic of bone remodeling, emphasizing how osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and osteocytes act as plastic network nodes whose state transitions are constrained by topology, compartmentalization, and metabolic/biophysical gating. We subsequently map macroscopic connectome architecture, detailing bidirectional axes coupling bone to the immune, metabolic, neural, and muscular systems. Within this framework, we systematically re-evaluate diverse skeletal disorders, spanning mechanometabolic degeneration, autoimmune disease, endocrine–metabolic fragility, and bone metastasis. We conceptualize these conditions as resulting from specific disruptions in systemic communication networks. From a translational perspective, this connectome paradigm guides the evaluation of precision therapeutics, such as targeted protein degradation and mRNA-based drugs, designed to rewire dysfunctional circuits. Finally, we discuss emerging concepts like digital skeletal twins and in silico clinical trials, highlighting their promising conceptual/translational status—rather than as established clinical tools—to eventually complement real-world evidence in future personalized regimen design. Significance Statement This review proposes the ‘skeletal connectome’ framework, redefining bone as a dynamic sensory and endocrine hub that integrates mechanical, metabolic, and immune circuits to sustain systemic homeostasis. By mapping diverse pathologies as characteristic network failure modes rather than isolated defects, this study outlines a translational roadmap for rewiring dysfunctional circuitry through precision perturbations—including mRNA therapeutics and targeted protein degradation—guided by digital skeletal twins.

title: Tri-driven graph reinforcement learning for dynamic root cause tracing in UF-RO water treatment processes
abstract: The ultrafiltration-reverse osmosis water treatment process is a highly coupled cyber-physical system vulnerable to cascading failures. To overcome the structural opacity, alarm floods, and limited spatial pathfinding of purely data-driven models, this study proposes a physics-data-knowledge tri-driven Graph Neural Network-Reinforcement Learning architecture, tailoring a dynamic sequential diagnostic framework specifically for UF-RO dual-membrane processes. At the data layer, a dual-driven quantification mechanism filters transient noise while preventing adaptive desensitization to progressive membrane fouling. Subsequently, by injecting physical piping layouts and expert rules as hard constraints, a high-fidelity grey-box physically plausible topology is constructed, effectively mitigating the spurious correlations prevalent in black-box methods. Powered by a Graph Attention Network for spatial perception, the Actor-Critic agent is guided by a multi-objective reward function strictly aligned with hydrodynamic propagation and physical attenuation laws. This mechanism compels the agent to execute autonomous, sequential dynamic inference across the constrained network. Validated against a two-year operational dataset from a full-scale 20,000 m3/d industrial plant, the model accurately converges to physical root causes with a 94.2% hit rate and reconstructs hydrodynamic propagation trajectories achieving an 89.7% path similarity. This study analyzes complex operational topologies, establishing a transparent, physically grounded diagnostic framework for smart water facilities.

title: Modal energy framework for multi-frequency oscillations in renewable grids
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy is accelerating the transition towards renewable-dominated and converter-rich power grids, while also introducing new stability challenges. Among these, multi-frequency oscillations have emerged as a major concern. Spanning frequencies from sub-hertz to kilohertz, arising from interactions among heterogeneous devices, control systems and networks, and evolving under continuously changing operating conditions, these oscillations are challenging to evaluate and mitigate within a unified framework, while also increasing the risk of instability, equipment overstress and maloperation of protection systems. In this Review, we summarize representative oscillation events and the four system-level characteristics of multi-frequency oscillations, assess existing methods for their evaluation and mitigation across different frequency ranges, and discuss the limitations of current approaches in capturing multimode coexistence, mode coupling and time-varying dynamics. Finally, we highlight a unified energy-based perspective as a promising basis for future advances in this field.

title: Forging certainty: A novel framework for the specification of combination products
abstract: The specification for a combination product represents a critical covenant of its quality. Too often, the current intellectual framework for forging this covenant remains a fragmented patchwork of legacy pharmaceutical and medical device paradigms. This paper argues that significant product failures are not random accidents but predictable consequences of these historical limitations. We therefore propose a novel, deductive framework—Quality by Design in Specification (QbD-S)—that complements existing empirical methods to address this systemic challenge. This paper presents a formal intellectual engine, the Universal Attribute Generator (UAG), which deconstructs therapeutic failure into five foundational Tenets and uses a rigorous "Interrogatory Filter" (Stress ' Capacity) to systematically derive a comprehensive set of quality attributes. This framework introduces the Criticality Vector to contextualize consequence by adding the dimension of "Context" to the standard scalar of "Severity," and mandates a Structured Falsification Protocol to build scientific confidence in its conclusions. The ultimate output is a "Master Control Strategy"—a binding regulatory mandate that legislates the "Fate" of each attribute, enabling either "Input-Controlled" Real-Time Release or mandating traditional "Symptom-Controlled" testing. QbD-S provides a systematic engine for translating patient needs into a scientifically rigorous and defensible covenant of quality.

title: Deep reinforcement learning empowers autonomous decision-making in intelligent air combat: challenges, breakthroughs, and prospects
abstract: With the accelerated evolution of modern air combat toward high dynamics and intense antagonism, the demand for autonomous decision-making capabilities in unmanned combat aerial vehicles has become increasingly urgent. Traditional methods based on empirical rules or simplified models can hardly meet the practical requirements of future intelligent air combat. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL), which integrates deep representation learning with sequential decision-making optimization, provides a highly promising technical paradigm for autonomous decision-making in complex environments. Focusing on the application of DRL in intelligent air combat, this paper systematically sorts out four core technical challenges under high-fidelity modeling scenarios: the modeling dilemmas of high-dimensional continuous state spaces and hybrid action spaces, the learning efficiency bottleneck caused by sparse rewards, the insufficient generalization and robustness of strategies, and the predicament of large-scale multi-agent cooperative decision-making. On this basis, this paper comprehensively summarizes the representative technological advances for addressing these challenges, including hierarchical reinforcement learning and time-scale separation methods, reward shaping and prior knowledge injection techniques, robust and generalized learning mechanisms, and multi-agent reinforcement learning frameworks for cooperative combat. Through systematic comparative analysis, the applicability and limitations of various technical routes in practical air combat scenarios are clarified. Finally, from the dimensions of explainability improvement, engineering deployment, and heterogeneous swarm collaboration, future development directions are prospected, providing a clear technical roadmap for relevant research in this field.

title: Adverse rotorcraft pilot couplings—Past, present and future challenges
abstract: Fixed and rotary wing pilots alike are familiar with potential instabilities or with annoying limit cycle oscillations that arise from the effort of controlling aircraft with high response actuation systems. Understanding, predicting and suppressing these inadvertent and sustained aircraft oscillations, known as aircraft (rotorcraft)-pilot couplings (A/RPCs) is a challenging problem for the designers. The goal of the present paper is to give an overview on the state-of-the-art in RPC problem, underlining the future challenges in this field. It is shown that, exactly as in the case of fixed wing APCs, RPCs existed from the beginning of rotorcraft development and that the problem of eliminating them is not yet solved: the current rotorcraft modelling for RPC analysis is rather limited to the particular case analysed and there is a lack of quantitative pilot behavioural models to analyse RPCs. The paper underlines the importance of involuntary pilot control actions, generally attributed to biodynamic couplings in predicting RPCs in rotorcraft. It is also shown that recent experiences demonstrate that modern rotorcraft seem to embed tendencies predisposing the flight control system FCS system towards dangerous RPCs. As the level of automation is likely to increase in future designs, extending to smaller aircraft and to different kinds of operation, the consequences of the pilot 'fighting' the FCS system and inducing A/RPCs needs to be eradicated. In Europe, the ARISTOTEL project (2010-2013) has been launched with the aim of understanding and predicting modern aircraft's susceptibility to A/RPC. The present paper gives an overview of future challenges to be solved for RPC-free design and some new solutions herein. © 2013 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Research progress and development prospects on critical challenges in deepwater riserless drill string dynamics
abstract: With the ongoing expansion of oil and gas drilling into deeper waters, riserless drilling technology has shown prominent advantages in deepwater drilling applications. The structural design and operational mechanism of riserless drilling make drill strings more vulnerable to stochastic ocean loads, requiring thorough investigation of critical factors influencing drill string dynamics in deepwater riserless operations to maintain drilling stability. Accordingly, this work initially synthesizes computational approaches for drill string external loads, elucidating how multiphysics-coupled loading mechanisms impact both drilling safety and operational efficiency. Furthermore, this work investigates fundamental challenges in drill string dynamics, including riser vortex-induced vibrations (VIV) in water columns and nonlinear drill string vibrations in formation sections, establishing connections between oceanic loads and traditional drilling dynamics. Moreover, this work systematically evaluates both active and passive vibration mitigation techniques, including VIV suppression for marine riser segments and formation vibration control methodologies. This work concludes by examining next-generation drilling control systems that feature intelligent data transmission, data-driven modeling, and smart control technologies. These elements collectively form a “perception-modeling-control” closed-loop system to overcome the time-delay limitations of traditional methods. The findings establish a theoretical foundation for deepwater drilling parameter optimization, safety risk mitigation, and efficiency improvement.

title: AgSentry: LiDAR reflectivity based obstacle detection for safety in agricultural environments
abstract: LiDAR is widely used for safety in agricultural robots, but the low resolution of cost-effective sensors limits long-range obstacle detection. This paper investigates how LiDAR reflectivity can be leveraged to improve safety perception on the ARWAC autonomous ground vehicle. We first evaluate a voxel-based emergency stop (E-STOP) system, quantifying braking distance, perception range, and processing delay to establish a reliable safety baseline. To enhance long-range obstacle detection, we propose a deep-learning pipeline that performs segmentation on LiDAR reflectivity images and projects the results onto corresponding 3D point clouds. We introduce AgSentry, an 850-image reflectivity dataset with five annotated obstacle classes common on farms. A controlled cross-architecture comparison of one-stage (YOLOv9), two-stage (Mask R-CNN), and transformer-based (RF-DETR) detectors demonstrates that reflectivity-based models consistently outperform their depth-based counterparts, with RF-DETR achieving the strongest overall results (mAP@50-95 of 29.88 vs. 24.53 for depth). The advantage is most pronounced for safety-critical classes: human detection mAP nearly doubles with reflectivity input (27.35 vs. 15.19), while vehicle detection improves by over 70%. These results demonstrate that reflectivity is an effective modality for improving long-distance safety perception in agricultural environments and motivate further integration with formal functional safety frameworks.

title: Control based on the Koopman operator: A comprehensive review
abstract: The Koopman operator provides a powerful linear framework for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems by lifting their behavior into a higher-dimensional space. This article presents a comprehensive review of the main methodologies for estimating the Koopman operator, with particular attention to forced systems–those influenced by external inputs. The approaches are organized into three primary categories: variants of Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), sparse regression techniques such as Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy), and data-driven methods based on deep neural networks. Building on this foundation, we propose a unified strategy for Koopman operator estimation and its integration into a model predictive control (MPC) framework. Using a multi-tank system as a case study, we show that the Koopman-based MPC yields a response that is twice as fast and significantly more stable under external disturbances–including fault conditions such as leaks–compared to a conventional linearized MPC. These results underscore the Koopman operator’s potential to enhance the modeling, control, and fault diagnosis of complex systems, offering a promising foundation for the development of robust, disturbance-tolerant predictive control architectures.

title: A comprehensive review on high-performance vapor chambers: Challenges, mechanisms, and future perspectives
abstract: Vapor chambers (VCs) have emerged as one of the most promising two-phase heat spreaders for next-generation electronics cooling, owing to their exceptional thermal conductivity, temperature uniformity, and compact form factor. However, the increasing power density of electronic devices ('500 W/cm2) and the trend toward ultra-thin packaging ('0.5 mm) impose stringent requirements on the wick structure, working fluid compatibility, and manufacturing precision. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in high-performance vapor chamber technology from the perspective of wick structure evolution, interfacial heat transfer enhancement, flow-channel optimization, and material–process integration. Homogeneous wicks (sintered powders, meshes, micro-grooves) are analyzed in terms of their intrinsic trade-off between capillary pressure and permeability, while composite and graded wicks achieve synergistic optimization through multiscale pore coordination. Emerging micro/nano-engineered and bioinspired wicks further enhance capillary transport and phase-change efficiency via hierarchical wettability and fractal fluid networks. In addition, advanced fabrication techniques—such as additive manufacturing, hybrid micro-etching, and laser sealing—enable high-precision, integrated VC architectures with improved mechanical robustness and gas-tight reliability. The emerging class of silicon- and ceramic-envelope (AlN, Al₂O₃) vapor chambers is also reviewed as a promising route for direct package-level thermal integration with CTE-matched semiconductor dies, offering an alternative to conventional copper-based integrated heat spreaders. Performance evaluation methods, including thermal resistance modeling, critical heat flux (CHF) characterization, and multi-physics simulations, are discussed to reveal governing limitations under extreme conditions. Finally, future directions are identified toward AI-assisted digital twin design, self-healing working fluids, and adaptive passive thermal control mechanisms, which are expected to progressively expand the operational envelope of vapor chambers toward ultrahigh heat flux regimes (potentially approaching '500 W/cm2 under optimized laboratory conditions) and broader environmental compatibility. This review provides a comprehensive framework linking materials, structures, and manufacturing to guide the development of next-generation high-performance vapor chambers for advanced thermal management applications.

title: Practices to identify and preclude adverse Aircraft-and-Rotorcraft-Pilot Couplings – A design perspective
abstract: Understanding, predicting and supressing the inadvertent aircraft oscillations caused by Aircraft/Rotorcraft Pilot Couplings (A/RPC) is a challenging problem for designers. These are potential instabilities that arise from the effort of controlling aircraft with high response actuation systems. The present paper reviews, updates and discusses desirable practices to be used during the design process for unmasking A/RPC phenomena. These practices are stemming from the European Commission project ARISTOTEL Aircraft and Rotorcraft Pilot Couplings - Tools and Techniques for Alleviation and Detection (2010-2013) and are mainly related to aerodynamic and structural modelling of the aircraft/rotorcraft, pilot modelling and A/RPC prediction criteria. The paper proposes new methodologies for precluding adverse A/RPCs events taking into account the aeroelasticity of the structure and pilot biodynamic interaction. It is demonstrated that high-frequency accelerations due to structural elasticity cause negative effects on pilot control, since they lead to involuntary body and limb-manipulator system displacements and interfere with pilot's deliberate control activity (biodynamic interaction) and, finally, worsen handling quality ratings.

title: Soft bioelectronics for diagnostic and therapeutic applications in neurological diseases
abstract: Physical and chemical signals in the central nervous system yield crucial information that is clinically relevant under both physiological and pathological conditions. The emerging field of bioelectronics focuses on the monitoring and manipulation of neurophysiological signals with high spatiotemporal resolution and minimal invasiveness. Significant advances have been realized through innovations in materials and structural design, which have markedly enhanced mechanical and electrical properties, biocompatibility, and overall device performance. The diagnostic and therapeutic potential of soft bioelectronics has been corroborated across a diverse array of pre-clinical settings. This review summarizes recent studies that underscore the developments and applications of soft bioelectronics in neurological disorders, including neuromonitoring, neuromodulation, tumor treatment, and biosensing. Limitations and outlooks of soft devices are also discussed in terms of power supply, wireless control, biocompatibility, and the integration of artificial intelligence. This review highlights the potential of soft bioelectronics as a future platform to promote deciphering brain functions and clinical outcomes of neurological diseases.

title: Advances in Hardware Reliability Assessment for Production Systems: A Review of Methods, Developments, Challenges and Future Perspectives
venue: Journal of Systems Science and Systems Engineering
abstract: Hardware Reliability Assessment HWRA has become essential in modern systems engineering due their increasing complexity. Traditional methods, including Markov models, Bayesian networks, fault tree analysis, reliability block diagrams, Petri nets and FMEA/FMECA, remain fundamental for reliability evaluation. However, Industry 4.0 technologies, including cyber-physical systems, digital twins, industrial IoT and data-driven decision support, expose limitations of conventional approaches. This paper presents a comprehensive critical review of HWRA methods, examining theoretical foundations, modelling capabilities and applications across production systems. It emphasizes dynamic reliability, multi-state systems, mission reliability, hybridization and integration with fuzzy logic, Monte Carlo simulation and data-driven techniques. Unlike previous reviews, it synthesizes the evolution of HWRA toward dynamic, hybrid and AI-enabled frameworks. The literature is analysed through challenges involving uncertainty, scalability, dynamic behaviour, emerging technologies and balance between realism and usability. Remaining gaps include computational burden, expert dependence and limited standardization, motivating future research directions emphasizing HWRA architectures.
